page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.4 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the instance in the middle tier for its hardware class. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a stress-ng single-core score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for uncached large block reads, and a write bandwidth of 36.66 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES.

In application-specific workloads, the instance achieves a Redis SET throughput of 34.66 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 23.2 GB/sec. Software compilation via Clang scores 28295.0 on Geekbench, while multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression reaches 161.64 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference handles 1928.13 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, and 57.07 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

This instance offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for compute-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent execution times, making it suitable for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, database operations, and medium-scale CPU-based inference tasks.
